content: Lock up your libraries if you like; but there is no gate, no lock, no bolt that you can set upon the freedom of my mind.
author: Virginia Woolf
story:
At its core, this reflection cuts through our everyday excuses. Holding onto anger is like clutching a glowing coal with the intent of throwing it at someone else—you are the one who gets burned. Retaliation only ties you tighter to the person who harmed you.

Virginia Woolf understood that real peace is never won by escaping the world or blaming external circumstances. Forgiveness and composure are not signs of weakness or giving someone a pass. They are acts of fierce self-preservation, cutting the emotional chain that allows another person's bad behavior to ruin your peace of mind.
reflectionPrompt: What creative idea or authentic voice have you held inside, and what small step can you take to express it?
